# Vekhanasa Sutta (MN 80 (PTS MN ii 40))

**ID:** MN 80 (PTS MN ii 40)
**Section:** Majjhimanikāya (mn)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-1
**Title (Pali):** Vekhanasa Sutta
**Title (English, from literature):** With Vekhanasa

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Vekhanasa Sutta* (MN 80) records a dialogue between the Buddha and the wanderer (*paribbājaka*) Vekhanasa [Law 1931; SuttaCentral]. The sutta begins in a manner closely parallel to the preceding *Cūḷasakuludāyi Sutta* (MN 79), with Vekhanasa engaging the Buddha in an exchange regarding the highest state and sensual pleasures [SuttaCentral; Law 1931]. The Buddha explains the nature of sensual pleasure based on the five cords of sensual desires (*rūpa*, *sadda*, *gandha*, *rasa*, and *phoṭṭhabba*), showing that one cannot attain conviction merely through clever debate, but rather through directly discerning the fruit of spiritual practice within oneself [Law 1931; SuttaCentral]. At the conclusion of MN 80, Vekhanasa declares himself satisfied and takes refuge as a lay disciple (*upāsaka*) [Law 1931; Sujato 2012].

Two full parallels are preserved in the Chinese Canon: a discourse in the *Madhyama-āgama* (MĀ 209) and an individual translation, the *Beimosu jing* (鞞摩肅經, T 90) [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. Whereas in MN 80 Vekhanasa only takes refuge as a lay follower, in MĀ 209 he is described as experiencing the vision of the Dhamma, going forth into homelessness, and ultimately attaining arahantship [Sujato 2012]. In his comparative study, Masaharu Anesaki also notes variations in the similes found in the Chinese counterparts, including additional similes of an oil lamp and fire following the simile of the infant [Anesaki 1908].

According to DharmaNexus match data, MN 80 shares substantial internal text reuse with MN 79 (longest shared section: §2.5–11.4 ↔ MN 79 §9.5–18.4), as well as significant shared passages with the *Poṭṭhapāda Sutta* (DN 9 §35–36), the *Tevijja Sutta* (DN 13 §19–20), and several discourses across the *Aṅguttara* and *Saṁyutta Nikāyas* [DharmaNexus]. It is also cited in the canonical commentary *Khaggavisāṇasuttaniddesa* (Cnd 23) [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. English translations have been made by I.B. Horner and Bhikkhu Sujato [SuttaCentral].
